/-!
# Erdős–Faber–Lovász conjecture

*Reference:* [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Erd%C5%91s%E2%80%93Faber%E2%80%93Lov%C3%A1sz_conjecture)
-/

namespace ErdosFaberLovaszConjecture

open scoped Classical in
/--
**Erdős–Faber–Lovász conjecture.** If $k$ complete graphs, each on exactly $k$ vertices,
have pairwise intersections of at most one vertex, then their union has a proper vertex coloring
with $k$ colors.

Here `C i` is the vertex set of the $i$th complete graph. The coloring is defined on the union of
these vertex sets, and being proper on each complete graph means that it is injective on `C i`.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 5]
theorem erdos_faber_lovasz_conjecture :
    ∀ (k : ℕ) (V : Type*) (C : Fin k → Finset V),
      (∀ i, (C i).card = k) →
      (∀ i j, i ≠ j → (C i ∩ C j).card ≤ 1) →
      ∃ c : {v : V // v ∈ Finset.univ.biUnion C} → Fin k,
        ∀ i, Set.InjOn c {v | (v : V) ∈ C i} := by
  sorry

end ErdosFaberLovaszConjecture
modeling_decisions: The terse list-page entry was made precise using the linked Wikipedia article's formulation: for every natural number k, there are k complete graphs, each with exactly k vertices, and distinct graphs share at most one vertex.

The k complete graphs are represented by their vertex sets as a family C : Fin k → Finset V. A complete graph is uniquely determined by its vertex set for the purpose of taking this union, so no bespoke graph structure is needed.

The vertices to be colored are the subtype of the actual union Finset.univ.biUnion C, rather than the whole ambient type V. This excludes unrelated ambient vertices and gives the correct empty domain when k = 0.

Proper coloring of the union is expressed as a map to Fin k that is injective on every C i. Since every edge in the union belongs to one of the complete graphs, this is exactly proper vertex coloring of that union.
The article's exact-k formulation was retained rather than the equivalent weakened formulation allowing clique size at most k.

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős–Faber–Lovász conjecture

The Erdős–Faber–Lovász conjecture (1972) is a problem on colouring unions of cliques. It says:
if $k$ complete graphs, each having exactly $k$ vertices, have the property that every pair of
complete graphs has at most one shared vertex, then the union of the graphs can be properly
coloured with $k$ colours.

The conjecture was proved for all sufficiently large $k$ by Kang, Kelly, Kühn, Methuku and
Osthus.

*References:*
- [Wikipedia, Erdős–Faber–Lovász conjecture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Erd%C5%91s%E2%80%93Faber%E2%80%93Lov%C3%A1sz_conjecture)
- [Wikipedia, List of unsolved problems in mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)
- [D. Y. Kang, T. Kelly, D. Kühn, A. Methuku, D. Osthus, *A proof of the Erdős–Faber–Lovász
  conjecture*, Ann. of Math. (2) 198 (2023)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2101.04698)
-/

open SimpleGraph
open scoped Finset

namespace ErdosFaberLovaszConjecture

/--
The union of the complete graphs on the vertex sets `A i`, as a graph on `V`: two distinct
vertices are adjacent if and only if they both belong to some `A i`.
-/
def unionOfCliques {ι V : Type*} (A : ι → Finset V) : SimpleGraph V :=
  fromRel fun u v => ∃ i, u ∈ A i ∧ v ∈ A i

@[category API, AMS 5]
theorem unionOfCliques_adj {ι V : Type*} (A : ι → Finset V) {u v : V} :
    (unionOfCliques A).Adj u v ↔ u ≠ v ∧ ∃ i, u ∈ A i ∧ v ∈ A i := by
  simp only [unionOfCliques, fromRel_adj]
  constructor
  · rintro ⟨huv, ⟨i, hu, hv⟩ | ⟨i, hv, hu⟩⟩ <;> exact ⟨huv, i, hu, hv⟩
  · rintro ⟨huv, i, hu, hv⟩
    exact ⟨huv, Or.inl ⟨i, hu, hv⟩⟩

/-- Each vertex set `A i` is a clique of `unionOfCliques A`. -/
@[category API, AMS 5]
theorem isClique_unionOfCliques {ι V : Type*} (A : ι → Finset V) (i : ι) :
    (unionOfCliques A).IsClique (A i) :=
  fun _ hu _ hv huv => (unionOfCliques_adj A).2 ⟨huv, i, hu, hv⟩

/-- `unionOfCliques A` is the smallest graph in which every `A i` is a clique. -/
@[category API, AMS 5]
theorem unionOfCliques_le_iff {ι V : Type*} (A : ι → Finset V) (G : SimpleGraph V) :
    unionOfCliques A ≤ G ↔ ∀ i, G.IsClique (A i) := by
  constructor
  · intro h i
    exact (isClique_unionOfCliques A i).mono h
  · intro h u v huv
    obtain ⟨hne, i, hu, hv⟩ := (unionOfCliques_adj A).1 huv
    exact h i hu hv hne

/-- A single clique on all of `V` gives the complete graph on `V`. -/
@[category test, AMS 5]
theorem unionOfCliques_univ {V : Type*} [Fintype V] :
    unionOfCliques (fun _ : Unit => (Finset.univ : Finset V)) = ⊤ := by
  ext u v
  simp [unionOfCliques_adj]

/--
**Erdős–Faber–Lovász conjecture.** If $k$ complete graphs, each having exactly $k$ vertices,
have the property that every pair of complete graphs has at most one shared vertex, then the
union of the graphs can be properly coloured with $k$ colours.

Here the $k$ complete graphs are the complete graphs on the vertex sets `A 0, …, A (k - 1)`,
each of size `k`, with `#(A i ∩ A j) ≤ 1` for `i ≠ j`. The type `V` is the vertex set of their
union, so every vertex of `V` lies in some `A i`; the union of the graphs is then
`unionOfCliques A`, and the conclusion is that it has a proper colouring with `k` colours.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 5]
theorem erdos_faber_lovasz_conjecture {V : Type*} [DecidableEq V] (k : ℕ) (A : Fin k → Finset V)
    (hcard : ∀ i, #(A i) = k)
    (hinter : ∀ i j, i ≠ j → #(A i ∩ A j) ≤ 1)
    (hcover : ∀ v, ∃ i, v ∈ A i) :
    (unionOfCliques A).Colorable k := by
  sorry

end ErdosFaberLovaszConjecture
attempts.decomposition_objections: None. The single-slot table matches the source: the list entry names one conjecture, and the article's committee, linear-hypergraph, intersection-graph and linear-intersection-number formulations are presented as equivalent reformulations rather than separate questions. Partial results and the unrestricted-intersection related problem are not posed by the statement.
modeling_decisions: The list-page entry only names the conjecture; the precise Prop is taken from the lead sentence of the Wikipedia article: k complete graphs, each with exactly k vertices, pairwise sharing at most one vertex, whose union is k-colourable. Wikipedia's 'exactly k' is used (hcard : #(A i) = k), not KKKMO's equivalent 'at most k'.

The k complete graphs are represented by their vertex sets A : Fin k → Finset V. The pairwise condition is imposed for distinct indices i ≠ j; for k ≥ 2 this forces the sets to be distinct, and for k ≤ 1 repetition is impossible/irrelevant, so indexing by Fin k is equivalent to a set of k distinct cliques.

The union of the graphs is modelled as the graph on V whose edges are the pairs of distinct vertices lying in a common A i (SimpleGraph.fromRel). Hypothesis hcover (every vertex of V lies in some A i) makes V exactly the vertex set of the union. This is needed so that the k = 0 case (no cliques, so the union has no vertices) is not falsified by stray isolated vertices in an ambient type; for k ≥ 1 it is equivalent to the version with arbitrary ambient V, since isolated vertices can be coloured freely.
'Can be properly coloured with k colours' is rendered as SimpleGraph.Colorable k (existence of a proper colouring with colours in Fin k), rather than chromaticNumber ≤ k; the two are equivalent.
[DecidableEq V] is assumed only to form the Finset intersection A i ∩ A j; it does not change the mathematical content.
Category is 'research open' per the given status; the module docstring notes the Kang–Kelly–Kühn–Methuku–Osthus proof for all sufficiently large k as background.

new_definitions.closest_existing_considered: SimpleGraph.completeGraph / ⊤ (only on a whole type), SimpleGraph.map of ⊤ along Function.Embedding.subtype (gives an unreadable ∃-∃ adjacency), ⨆ of such maps, SimpleGraph.IsClique (a predicate, not a construction), and sInf {H | ∀ i, H.IsClique (A i)} (correct but opaque).
new_definitions.name: ErdosFaberLovaszConjecture.unionOfCliques
new_definitions.why_needed: The conjecture is about the union of the complete graphs on given vertex sets A i inside a common vertex type. Mathlib has no construction of 'the complete graph on a subset s ⊆ V' as a SimpleGraph V, nor of a union of such cliques; unionOfCliques A := SimpleGraph.fromRel (fun u v => ∃ i, u ∈ A i ∧ v ∈ A i) is exactly this union. API lemmas (adjacency characterisation, each A i is a clique, it is the least graph in which every A i is a clique) and a test (a single clique on univ gives ⊤) are proved in the file.

erdos_faber_lovasz_conjecture.why: Stated as: for every k, every vertex type V, and every family A : Fin k → Finset V with #(A i) = k, #(A i ∩ A j) ≤ 1 for i ≠ j, and every vertex of V in some A i, the graph unionOfCliques A (edges = pairs of distinct vertices in a common A i) is k-colourable (SimpleGraph.Colorable k). This is the Wikipedia formulation with 'exactly k vertices' and 'at most one shared vertex'. A bespoke definition unionOfCliques was needed because Mathlib has no 'complete graph on a vertex subset / union of cliques' construction.

If $k$ complete graphs, each on exactly $k$ vertices, have pairwise intersections of at most one
vertex, then their union has a proper coloring with $k$ colors. Here `cliques i` is the vertex set
of the $i$th complete graph, the coverage hypothesis says that `V` is their union, and injectivity
of `color` on every `cliques i` expresses proper coloring of the union.

    ∀ (k : ℕ) (V : Type*) (cliques : Fin k → Set V),

      (∀ i j, i ≠ j → (cliques i ∩ cliques j).encard ≤ 1) →
      (∀ v, ∃ i, v ∈ cliques i) →
      ∃ color : V → Fin k, ∀ i, Set.InjOn color (cliques i) := by
  sorry

end ErdosFaberLovaszConjecture
modeling_decisions: Represented the k complete graphs by a family `cliques : Fin k → Set V` of their vertex sets. Since a complete graph is determined by its vertex set, proper coloring of the union is equivalent to requiring the color function to be injective on every member of this family.
Used `Set.encard` rather than `Set.ncard`: `(cliques i).encard = k` faithfully means exactly k vertices and rules out infinite sets, while `ncard` alone has a default value on infinite sets.

Required `∀ v, ∃ i, v ∈ cliques i` so that the ambient type `V` is exactly the vertex set of the union, rather than allowing unrelated isolated vertices. This also gives the correct empty union when `k = 0`.

Interpreted 'colored with k colors' as existence of a coloring into `Fin k` (at most k colors), without an explicit surjectivity requirement. For positive k, each k-vertex clique and injectivity force all k colors to occur anyway.
Formalized the precise declarative formulation from the dedicated Wikipedia article because the list-page source only names the conjecture.

/-!
# Erdős–Faber–Lovász conjecture

The Erdős–Faber–Lovász conjecture on coloring unions of cliques.

*References:*
- [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Erd%C5%91s%E2%80%93Faber%E2%80%93Lov%C3%A1sz_conjecture)
- [Wikipedia, List of unsolved problems in mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)
- D. Y. Kang, T. Kelly, D. Kühn, A. Methuku, D. Osthus,
  *A proof of the Erdős–Faber–Lovász conjecture*, Ann. of Math. 198 (2023), 537–618.
  [arXiv:2101.04698](https://arxiv.org/abs/2101.04698)
-/

namespace ErdosFaberLovaszConjecture

open SimpleGraph

/--
**Erdős–Faber–Lovász conjecture.**
If $k$ complete graphs, each having exactly $k$ vertices, have the property that every pair of
complete graphs has at most one shared vertex, then the union of the graphs can be properly
colored with $k$ colors.

Here the $i$-th complete graph has vertex set `C i`, so its edges are all pairs of distinct
vertices of `C i`, and the union of the graphs is `⨆ i, (completeGraph (C i : Set V)).spanningCoe`.
The vertex set of this union is the union of the `C i`, so the hypothesis `∀ v, ∃ i, v ∈ C i`
says that the vertex type `V` is exactly this vertex set.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 5]
theorem erdos_faber_lovasz_conjecture {V : Type*} [DecidableEq V] (k : ℕ) (C : Fin k → Finset V)
    (hcard : ∀ i, (C i).card = k)
    (hinter : Pairwise fun i j => (C i ∩ C j).card ≤ 1)
    (hcover : ∀ v, ∃ i, v ∈ C i) :
    (⨆ i, (completeGraph (C i : Set V)).spanningCoe).Colorable k := by
  sorry

end ErdosFaberLovaszConjecture
attempts.decomposition_objections: None. The single slot is the natural content of the list entry; the equivalent reformulations (committees, linear hypergraph chromatic index, intersection graphs, linear intersection number) are indeed the same question and need not be separate slots.
modeling_decisions: Precise formulation taken from the article's lead sentence (the list entry only names the conjecture): k complete graphs on exactly k vertices each, pairwise sharing at most one vertex, union is k-colorable. The 'exactly k vertices' reading of Wikipedia is used, not KKKMO's 'at most k' variant.

Cliques are represented by their vertex sets `C : Fin k → Finset V` (indexed by Fin k, so there are exactly k of them, possibly with repetition; for k ≥ 2 the intersection hypothesis forces them to be distinct, and for k ≤ 1 repetition is harmless). The i-th complete graph is `(completeGraph (C i : Set V)).spanningCoe`, and the union is the lattice supremum `⨆ i` in `SimpleGraph V`. I verified in a scratch file that its adjacency is `u ≠ v ∧ ∃ i, u ∈ C i ∧ v ∈ C i`.

The hypothesis `hcover : ∀ v, ∃ i, v ∈ C i` makes the vertex type V exactly the vertex set of the union of the cliques (as in the informal statement, where 'the union of the graphs' has vertex set ⋃ C i). Without it, the statement would be false in the degenerate case k = 0 with V nonempty (the empty graph on a nonempty type is not 0-colorable), while for k ≥ 1 it is equivalent to the version without hcover (isolated vertices do not affect k-colorability). hcover also makes V finite automatically.

'Every pair of complete graphs has at most one shared vertex' is `Pairwise fun i j => (C i ∩ C j).card ≤ 1`, i.e. only for i ≠ j; `[DecidableEq V]` is assumed only so that Finset intersection is available.
Conclusion is `Colorable k` (existence of a proper coloring with colors in Fin k) rather than `chromaticNumber ≤ k`; these are equivalent by `SimpleGraph.chromaticNumber_le_iff_colorable`.

Category `research open` as required by the task status, although the article notes the conjecture was proved for all sufficiently large k by Kang–Kelly–Kühn–Methuku–Osthus (the full conjecture for all k remains open).

erdos_faber_lovasz_conjecture.why: Stated with existing Mathlib primitives only: the k cliques are given by their vertex sets C : Fin k → Finset V with (C i).card = k, pairwise intersections of card ≤ 1 (Pairwise, i.e. i ≠ j), the union of the complete graphs is ⨆ i, (completeGraph (C i : Set V)).spanningCoe : SimpleGraph V, and 'properly colored with k colors' is SimpleGraph.Colorable k (equivalent to chromaticNumber ≤ k via chromaticNumber_le_iff_colorable). A hypothesis ∀ v, ∃ i, v ∈ C i fixes V to be exactly the vertex set of the union.

/-!
# Erdős–Faber–Lovász conjecture

If $k$ complete graphs, each having exactly $k$ vertices, have the property that every pair of
complete graphs has at most one shared vertex, then the union of the graphs can be properly
colored with $k$ colors.

The conjecture was formulated by Erdős, Faber and Lovász in 1972. Kang, Kelly, Kühn, Methuku and
Osthus proved it for all sufficiently large $k$.

*References:*
- [Wikipedia: Erdős–Faber–Lovász conjecture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Erd%C5%91s%E2%80%93Faber%E2%80%93Lov%C3%A1sz_conjecture)
- [Wikipedia: List of unsolved problems in mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)
- [KKKMO23] Kang, D. Y., Kelly, T., Kühn, D., Methuku, A., Osthus, D.,
  *A proof of the Erdős–Faber–Lovász conjecture*, Ann. of Math. (2) 198 (2023), 537–618.
  [arXiv:2101.04698](https://arxiv.org/abs/2101.04698)
-/

open SimpleGraph

/--
Two vertices are adjacent in the union of the complete graphs on the vertex sets `C i` if and
only if they are distinct and both lie in some `C i`.
-/
@[category API, AMS 5]
lemma iSup_fromRel_adj {V : Type*} {k : ℕ} (C : Fin k → Finset V) (u v : V) :
    (⨆ i, fromRel fun u v => u ∈ C i ∧ v ∈ C i).Adj u v ↔
      u ≠ v ∧ ∃ i, u ∈ C i ∧ v ∈ C i := by
  simp only [iSup_adj, fromRel_adj]
  constructor
  · rintro ⟨i, hne, h | h⟩
    · exact ⟨hne, i, h⟩
    · exact ⟨hne, i, h.2, h.1⟩
  · rintro ⟨hne, i, h⟩
    exact ⟨i, hne, Or.inl h⟩

/--
Each vertex set `C i` of cardinality `k` is a `k`-clique of the union of the complete graphs.
-/
@[category test, AMS 5]
lemma isNClique_iSup_fromRel {V : Type*} {k : ℕ} (C : Fin k → Finset V)
    (hcard : ∀ i, (C i).card = k) (i : Fin k) :
    (⨆ i, fromRel fun u v => u ∈ C i ∧ v ∈ C i).IsNClique k (C i) := by
  refine ⟨fun u hu v hv huv => ?_, hcard i⟩
  simp only [iSup_adj, fromRel_adj]
  exact ⟨i, huv, Or.inl ⟨hu, hv⟩⟩

/--
**Erdős–Faber–Lovász conjecture.** If $k$ complete graphs, each having exactly $k$ vertices,
have the property that every pair of complete graphs has at most one shared vertex, then the
union of the graphs can be properly colored with $k$ colors.

Here the $k$ complete graphs have vertex sets `C 0, …, C (k - 1)`, each of cardinality `k`, and
two distinct complete graphs share at most one vertex. The vertex type `V` is the union of these
vertex sets (hypothesis `hcover`). The union of the complete graphs is the graph on `V` in which
two distinct vertices are adjacent exactly when they both lie in some `C i`, i.e.
`⨆ i, fromRel fun u v => u ∈ C i ∧ v ∈ C i`. The conclusion is that this graph has a proper
coloring with `k` colors.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 5]
theorem erdos_faber_lovasz_conjecture {V : Type*} [DecidableEq V] (k : ℕ) (C : Fin k → Finset V)
    (hcard : ∀ i, (C i).card = k)
    (hinter : ∀ i j, i ≠ j → (C i ∩ C j).card ≤ 1)
    (hcover : ∀ v, ∃ i, v ∈ C i) :
    (⨆ i, fromRel fun u v => u ∈ C i ∧ v ∈ C i).Colorable k := by
  sorry

end ErdosFaberLovaszConjecture

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős–Faber–Lovász conjecture

The Erdős–Faber–Lovász conjecture (1972) is a problem about coloring unions of cliques. It says:
if $k$ complete graphs, each having exactly $k$ vertices, have the property that every pair of
complete graphs has at most one shared vertex, then the union of the graphs can be properly
colored with $k$ colors.

Kang, Kelly, Kühn, Methuku and Osthus proved the conjecture for all sufficiently large $k$.
The conjecture for every $k$ remains open.

*References:*
- [Wikipedia, Erdős–Faber–Lovász conjecture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Erd%C5%91s%E2%80%93Faber%E2%80%93Lov%C3%A1sz_conjecture)
- [Wikipedia, List of unsolved problems in mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)
- [KKKMO23] Kang, D. Y., Kelly, T., Kühn, D., Methuku, A., Osthus, D.,
  *A proof of the Erdős–Faber–Lovász conjecture*. Ann. of Math. (2) 198 (2023), 537–618.
  [arXiv:2101.04698](https://arxiv.org/abs/2101.04698)
-/

namespace ErdosFaberLovaszConjecture

/--
**Erdős–Faber–Lovász conjecture.** If $k$ complete graphs, each having exactly $k$ vertices,
have the property that every pair of complete graphs has at most one shared vertex, then the
union of the graphs can be properly colored with $k$ colors.

The $k$ complete graphs are given by their vertex sets $A_1, \dots, A_k$: finite sets of
vertices of size exactly $k$ such that $|A_i \cap A_j| \le 1$ for $i \ne j$. The union of the
complete graphs is the graph whose vertex set is $\bigcup_i A_i$ (the type `V`, by `hcover`)
and in which two distinct vertices are adjacent iff they lie in a common $A_i$. The conjecture
states that this graph has a proper coloring with $k$ colors.
-/

theorem erdos_faber_lovasz_conjecture {V : Type*} [DecidableEq V] (k : ℕ) (A : Fin k → Finset V)
    (hcard : ∀ i, (A i).card = k)
    (hinter : ∀ i j, i ≠ j → (A i ∩ A j).card ≤ 1)
    (hcover : ∀ v, ∃ i, v ∈ A i) :
    (SimpleGraph.fromRel fun u v => ∃ i, u ∈ A i ∧ v ∈ A i).Colorable k := by

end ErdosFaberLovaszConjecture

modeling_decisions: The list entry only names the conjecture; the precise Prop is the Wikipedia article's lead formulation: k complete graphs with exactly k vertices each, pairwise sharing at most one vertex, union is k-colorable (not KKKMO's 'at most k vertices' variant, and not the hypergraph/intersection-graph reformulations).

vertex, then their union has a proper coloring with $k$ colors. Here `C i` is the vertex set of the

      ∃ coloring : {v : V // ∃ i, v ∈ C i} → Fin k,
        ∀ i, Set.InjOn coloring {v | (v : V) ∈ C i} := by

Represented the exactly k complete graphs by a family C : Fin k → Finset V, with each C i having cardinality exactly k; this follows Wikipedia's exact-size formulation rather than the at-most-k equivalent variant mentioned in the decomposition notes.

Took the coloring domain to be the subtype of vertices belonging to at least one C i, exactly the vertex set of the union. This also handles k = 0 correctly without imposing coloring obligations on unrelated ambient vertices.

Expressed proper coloring of the union by requiring a map to Fin k to be injective on every clique C i. Since the union's edges are exactly the pairs of distinct vertices sharing a clique, this is equivalent to a proper k-coloring.
